stem.text: Sand is added to a pile at a work site at the rate \( r(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} + 9 \) tons per hour, and removed at the constant rate of 7 tons per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 24 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 50 tons of sand in the pile, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 24 \) at which the amount A(t) of sand is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 6.769, where A is 100.964 tons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 24.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 50 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{12} \right)} + 2\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = r(t) - 7 = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} + 2 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 6.769 \) and \( t = 17.231 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 50 \), \( A(6.769) \approx 100.964 \), \( A(17.231) \approx 47.036 \), and \( A(24) = 50 + \int_{0}^{24} A'(s)\,ds = 98 \).
The largest candidate value is about 100.964, at the first critical point, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 6.769 \) hours.

The amount is greatest at t = 24, where A is 98 tons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at t = 17.231 and at t = 24.

options.label: The amount is greatest at t = 24, where A is 98 tons, because A' is positive on the interval from t = 17.231 to t = 24.
options.derivation: a local argument at the right end: A' is positive just before the endpoint, so A is taken to be greatest there
